questions.title: Which company will hold the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign firm as of July 10, 2026?
questions.background: Alibaba's 2014 US initial public offering raised $25 billion, setting the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign company.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official issuer announcements and contemporaneous reporting by reputable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the company reported as holding the all-time record for the largest US initial public offering by a foreign company as of July 10, 2026. Compare offerings by proceeds raised, not company valuation. An offering whose pricing and share sales have been announced may qualify before exchange trading begins. Accepted Answer Format : The company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: Monday June 29 Korea Herald and Korea Times reporting shows further erosion in SK Hynix's USD IPO cushion amid renewed US-Iran strikes and record foreign selling (7.73 trillion won net foreign outflow on Monday): SK Hynix fell another 1.68% to close at 2.62 million won (after dropping 8.36% Friday), while the won weakened to 1,544.45/USD. At 2.62M won and 1,544.45 KRW/USD, the 17.79M new shares imply 46.61T won ($30.18B, down from $31.0B Friday; board cap of 45.45T won = $29.43B), narrowing the cushion over Alibaba's $25.0B record from 19.6% to 17.2%—still clearing $25B under a standard 10-15% ADR discount ($25.65B-$27.16B). While July 10 Nasdaq debut plans remain on track alongside bullish Mirae Asset inflow projections ($4.5B passive inflows) and Korea's $520B chip-cluster announcement, extreme KOSPI volatility (weekly options postponed), sustained foreign outflows, and a tight ~8 US trading-day calendar (with the July 3 holiday) trim SK Hynix from 0.66 to 0.63 and lift Alibaba from 0.33 to 0.37 (removing the 1% residual tail since no other foreign firm can launch a >$25B US IPO by July 10).

questions.title: Which ownership group will receive NFL owners' approval to buy the Seattle Seahawks in 2026?
questions.background: The Seattle Seahawks are owned by Paul Allen's estate. Allen's will calls for the team to be sold and the assets distributed to charities.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official NFL announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the purchasing group approved by NFL owners. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the purchasing ownership group in the first sale of the Seattle Seahawks formally approved by NFL owners during 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the purchasing group or the family leading it.
questions.current_reasoning: June 29 Seattle Times coverage citing Bloomberg News reports that first-round bids to buy the Seattle Seahawks were due Monday, June 29 (earlier than previously rumored July 6), that no new potential buyers have emerged beyond the three previously identified groups (Aditya Mittal & Wyc Grousbeck, Todd Boehly, and Vinod Khosla), and that the bidder pool is 'fairly shallow' and 'shrinking' as the record $9B-$10B valuation tests billionaires' cash appetite. questions.title: If Morgan Rogers leaves Aston Villa during the 2026 summer transfer window, which club will he join?
questions.background: Morgan Rogers is an England international and an attacking player for Aston Villa.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from either club confirming a completed permanent transfer, corroborated by reputable sports reporting. Resolution Conditions : Conditional on Rogers completing a permanent transfer away from Aston Villa during the 2026 summer transfer window, resolve to the acquiring club. If he completes multiple transfers during the window, use his first permanent transfer from Aston Villa. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the acquiring football club.
questions.current_reasoning: Conditional on Morgan Rogers completing a permanent exit from Aston Villa, Premier League champions Arsenal are the overwhelming frontrunners across June 20-24 reporting (The Times, Guardian, Daily Mail, Ben Jacobs, Nicolo Schira), with Mikel Arteta and Andrea Berta prioritizing him and Declan Rice recruiting him in England's World Cup camp. Villa's £85m-£100m valuation (amplified by Middlesbrough's 20% sell-on clause) restricts the buyer pool to a handful of elite clubs, with Chelsea (long-standing Joe Shields link), Manchester City (former academy club refreshing under Enzo Maresca), PSG, and Manchester United the main hijack threats.

questions.title: Which club will sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig in summer 2026?
questions.background: Yan Diomande is an Ivory Coast winger playing for RB Leipzig.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by RB Leipzig or the destination club confirming an agreement for Diomande's permanent transfer. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the destination club in the first such agreement announced between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Loan agreements do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the destination club.

questions.title: Which player will command the highest transfer fee paid by a Premier League club during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: This question concerns completed transfers into Premier League clubs ahead of the 2026–27 season.

The answer is the player whose transfer fee, expressed in pounds sterling, is the highest paid by a Premier League club during that window. Exclude proposed or failed transfers. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.

questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
questions.background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Qualifying Event : Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify. Source of Truth : Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the state.
questions.current_reasoning: According to the Rockefeller Institute's June 10, 2026 tracker of 14 states weighing data center moratoria, Maine's bill was vetoed by Gov. Janet Mills on April 24 (override failed April 29), leaving New York as the ONLY state whose legislature has passed a statewide moratorium (a compromise 1-year freeze on >=20 MW facilities passed both chambers June 4). Gov. Kathy Hochul faces re-election in November 2026 amid intense utility-bill pushback and signaled openness ('the status quo can't continue'), giving New York a commanding lead (including potential signing with chapter amendments). If Hochul vetoes, full-time legislatures still in session (Michigan, Pennsylvania) or states with prior momentum or executive options (Maine, Virginia, plus ~11% across California, New Jersey, Massachusetts, and others) remain secondary contenders.

questions.title: With which country will the United States record its largest trade deficit in May 2026?
questions.background: The United States publishes monthly trade data, including trade balances with its major trading partners.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve using the country-level trade balances in the initial May 2026 trade report from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau. Identify the individual country associated with the largest U.S. trade deficit, excluding regional groupings. Resolution Date : 2026-07-07 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: In BEA/Census Exhibit 19 monthly goods balances (the only country-level data in monthly releases), Taiwan and Vietnam dominated Q1-April 2026: Taiwan led March ($20.6B vs Vietnam $19.2B, Mexico $16.4B, China $14.0B) and Q1 ($59.1B vs $54.2B), and tied Vietnam at $19.3B in April (listed first by BEA) well ahead of Mexico ($14.8B) and China ($12.0B). Partner May 2026 trade releases from early June show Taiwan's total exports surging back to $78.48B (second-highest ever, near March's $80.18B record, with $22.94B to the U.S. +47.9% YoY), while Vietnam's total exports rose +2.1% MoM and China's customs surplus with the U.S. rebounded +$2.95B to $26.02B. Given seasonal-adjustment swings of $1-2B, Taiwan is favored over a very close Vietnam, with smaller tails for China and Mexico.
